question: Why should one act without attachment to fruits?
premises: your right is in action not fruits
do not be cause of action-fruit
be engaged in action only not fruits
if pervaded by fruit-desire impurity then action becomes cause of fruit
unasked fruit is knowing not for unwilling
attachment through inaction is false knowing to be abandoned
inference: Action without fruit-desire preserves non-causal knowing; inaction-attachment is false knowing.
plain_english: Therefore your right is in action, never in fruits; do not be cause of action-fruit, and let no attachment be in inaction. Be engaged in action only, not in fruits. Surely action done necessarily brings fruit? Not so: if you are pervaded by fruit-desire impurity, then action becomes cause of fruit; unasked fruit is knowing, not for the unwilling. Attachment through absence of action is firm-grasp false knowing, to be abandoned indeed.
